question: How often should I meet with my advisor?
response:
According to the Advising FAQ, you are required to meet with your advisor each semester before class registration and before you declare a major [6]. Your advisor might also arrange additional advising sessions throughout the semester [6]. You are encouraged to be in touch with your advisor and reach out any time you have questions or concerns [6].

---

question: When can I declare a major?
response:
You may declare a major as early as the beginning of fall term of your sophomore year [2]. You may declare a major in the spring term of your sophomore year [1]. All students must secure formal approval of their long-range plans and declare a major no later than the last teaching day of the first seven-week session in their fourth semester/term [1][2].

---

**Sources**
- [1] Advising FAQ (12-19-24 Update).docx
- [2] ug_bulletin_2025-2026.pdf

question: What is the process for major declaration?
response:
At Duke Kunshan University, all undergraduate students enter without a major and are assigned an academic advisor [1]. In the sophomore year, students preparing to declare a major work with their advisors—and potentially others who have advised them—to develop a long-range academic plan [1]. This plan lays out the courses they anticipate taking in their remaining terms and is reviewed by their advisor to confirm that it will meet established graduation requirements [1]. Students may declare a major as early as the beginning of fall term of the sophomore year, but all students must secure formal approval of their long-range plans and declare a major no later than the last teaching day of the first seven-week session in their fourth term [1]. Until then, students should explore different major options to make the best choice for themselves [1]. Students who do not declare their major may be prevented from registering for classes for their fifth undergraduate term and from participating in a term or study away program [1]. Students who have declared a major and wish to change it may do so by submitting a form to the Office of the Registrar [1]. No changes in majors can be made after the end of the Drop/Add period of the first session of the fall term in the senior year [1].

---

**Sources**
- [1] ug_bulletin_2025-2026.pdf

question: What are the Distribution Requirements?
response:
DKU’s undergraduate distribution requirement requires at least 4 credits in each of the three divisional areas: Arts and Humanities (AH), Natural and Applied Sciences (NAS), and Social Sciences (SS) [7][10]. It consists of 3 courses, 12 credits total [8]. Courses that fulfill the distribution requirement are designated by divisional area attributes [7][8]. A student may fulfill the distribution requirement in a divisional area by taking one 4-credit course or two 2-credit courses with that divisional area attribute [7]. The distribution requirement cannot be fulfilled with AP or IPC credits [7]. Courses with two divisional area attributes can only be counted as one area attribute [7][10]. Courses with both a Quantitative Reasoning (QR) attribute and a divisional area attribute can only be counted as one of these attributes [7]. Courses with both a Writing (W) attribute and a divisional area attribute can only be counted as one of these attributes [7]. Transfer credit from Duke or other academic institutions through study abroad or summer programs needs review and approval from the division chair to fulfill the distributional requirement [7]. The Advising FAQ adds that you cannot use one class for two distribution requirements even if the course has both attributes [10].

---

**Sources**
- [7][8] ug_bulletin_2025-2026.pdf
- [10] Advising FAQ (12-19-24 Update).docx

question: How many credits can I take in a semester?
response:
The normal course load is 16–20 credits per semester (8–10 credits in each 7-week session) [1]. A course overload is defined as enrolling in more than 20 credits in a semester, exclusive of PE, up to 24 credits [1]. As a freshman, you are required to enroll in a maximum of 8 credits for the first session of your first semester [1]. If you are on academic probation, you may register for no more than 16 credits plus one PE course [1].

---

**Sources**
- [1] Advising FAQ (12-19-24 Update).docx

question: When is the deadline to withdraw from a class?
response:
Fall 2025: the last day to withdraw with a W grade is Thursday, September 18, 2025 for first 7-week classes [6]; Thursday, November 6, 2025 for 14-week classes [6]; and Thursday, November 20, 2025 for second 7-week classes [8].  
Spring 2026: the last day to withdraw with a W grade is Thursday, February 5, 2026 for first 7-week classes [11]; Thursday, April 2, 2026 for 14-week classes [11]; and Thursday, April 16, 2026 for second 7-week classes [10].

question: What letter grade would be considered CR and what would be considered NC?
response:
A grade of C- or better is considered CR (Credit), and a grade of D+ or below is considered NC (No Credit) [2].

---

**Sources**
- [2] Advising FAQ (12-19-24 Update).docx

question: When do I get assigned an Incomplete (I) grade?
response:
An Incomplete (I) grade may be assigned when, because of illness, emergency, or circumstances outside your reasonable control, you cannot complete the work for a course or cannot attend the final examination [2][5]. In that situation, you may request the assignment of an I in writing to the instructor [2][5]. The UG Bulletin adds that you are also expected to discuss the I grade with your academic advisor [5].

An incomplete grade will not be authorized if you have a history of excessive absences or failure to complete coursework in a timely fashion [2][5]. Once an I grade is assigned, the course must be completed and you can no longer withdraw from the course [5].

---

**Sources**
- [2] Advising FAQ (12-19-24 Update).docx
- [5] ug_bulletin_2025-2026.pdf

question: How many credits of foreign language courses are required?
response:
The language-course requirement is 8–16 credits overall [1][3]. Students in the English for Academic Purposes (EAP) track are required to complete eight credits of EAP courses—EAP 101A to EAP 102B—and may also take elective 200+ level EAP or WOC courses [1]. Students in the Chinese as a Second Language (CSL) track need to complete 8–16 credits of Chinese courses appropriate to their Chinese skill level [1]. Students who are not assigned to either the EAP track or the CSL track can satisfy their foreign language requirement by taking advanced written and oral communication (WOC) courses, or courses in an additional language [1][5].

---

**Sources**
- [1][3][5] ug_bulletin_2025-2026.pdf

question: What are the three Common Core courses and in which year is each taken?
response:
The three Common Core courses and their designated years are:

- China in the World (Year 1) [1][2]
- Global Challenges in Science, Technology and Health (Year 2) [1][2]
- Ethics, Citizenship and the Examined Life (Year 3) [1][2]
